title: Classic Pot Roast with Carrots & Potatoes
subtitle: a Sunday beef roast braised low and slow until it falls apart, with carrots, potatoes and rich gravy
imageAlt: Tender pulled pot roast with carrots and potatoes in brown gravy on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for two, plus 4 lunches or a second dinner

beforeYouStart.text: A frozen roast needs about 2 days in the fridge to thaw.
You need an oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy pot with a lid, about 5.5 L.

items.name: boneless beef blade or cross rib roast

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Pat the roast dry and season all over with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the roast well on all sides, 10–12 minutes. Lift it onto a plate.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Lower to medium. Cook the onion 3 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute. Pour in the broth and Worcestershire, scraping up the brown bits, and add the dried thyme and bay leaves.

steps.title: Braise
steps.text: Return the roast and any juices, bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven 2 hours.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Tuck the carrots and potatoes around the roast, sprinkle with the salt, cover and braise 1–1¼ hours more, until the beef pulls apart with a fork, about 90°C (195°F), well past the safe 63°C (145°F), and the vegetables are tender.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Lift the beef and vegetables onto a platter and tent with foil. Discard the bay leaves, skim the fat, then bring the liquid to a boil on the stove and stir in the cornstarch mix. Simmer 1–2 minutes until glossy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pull the beef into large chunks and serve with the vegetables and plenty of gravy.

fixIt.fix: It needs more time, not more heat. Cover and braise 30 minutes more, then check again.
Add another 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with water and simmer 1 minute.
Cut them bigger next time, or add them 15 minutes later.

saleTip: Blade and cross rib roasts often drop to about $11/kg in No Frills sales; buy one and freeze it.
swap: Slow cooker: after searing and making the base, cook on low 8–9 hours with the vegetables underneath, then thicken the gravy on the stove.
leftovers: Shred leftover beef into the gravy for hot beef sandwiches.
doneness: Whole cuts of beef are safe from 63°C (145°F) (Health Canada); pot roast is braised on to about 90°C (195°F) so it falls apart.
source: Based on tested Dutch-oven pot roast methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): a seared blade roast braised in beef broth at 160°C for about 3 hours, vegetables added for the last hour, gravy thickened with cornstarch.
gear: Dutch oven or heavy oven-safe pot with lid (5.5 L)
prepAhead: Make it a day ahead and chill in the gravy; lift off the fat and reheat covered at 160°C (325°F) for 40 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).
Peel and cut the carrots up to 2 days ahead.
reheat: Covered with gravy over medium, or in the microwave 2–3 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beef, potatoes and carrots in broth gravy; no Worcestershire, dried thyme or bay.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the Worcestershire, dried thyme and bay leaves.
stepNotes.4: Basic: nothing to discard; just skim and thicken.

fancy.note: A splash of red wine in the braise and butter whisked into the gravy.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: pour in the wine after the tomato paste and boil 2 minutes before adding the broth.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: whisk the butter into the finished gravy.

plating: Serve family-style on a big platter.

why.0-0: Blade and cross rib have lots of connective tissue that melts into tender, juicy meat with long, low heat.
why.0-6: Browned tomato paste gives the gravy colour and depth.
why.2-0: Cornstarch thickens the gravy in a minute without lumps.

funFact: Braising (browning, then cooking low and covered in a little liquid) comes from the French 'braise', the hot coals once piled on the pot's lid.

keeps.note: freeze the beef in its gravy
